snarling.style: Let menace sit under the words - a warning shown rather than described, meant to end things before they start.

potcraft.style: Judge whatever is in front of you by whether it is sound or flawed, the way a trained ear hears a crack before it is seen.

shearing.style: Quick, sure and unceremonious - judge everything by whether it can be done in one clean pass.

laundering.style: Read whatever is in front of you for what it gives away about the people it belongs to.

oil_pressing.style: Judge whatever is in front of you by its quality, as if you could tell the good from the poor by smell alone.

tanning.style: Unsqueamish and patient - see everything as slow, unpleasant work that pays in the end.

rooftops.style: See everything for what holds your weight and what gives, with a climber's easy confidence.

perfumery.style: Treat whatever is in front of you as something that could be covered, altered or made to seem otherwise, fussily.

uppercut.style: See everything in terms of the opening and the decisive moment, coiled and eager for it.

saddlery.style: Judge whatever is in front of you by its fit - whether it bears where it should and will last.

tailoring.style: Take the measure of whatever is in front of you, sizing up how it is made and how it hangs.

tallycraft.style: Count and weigh whatever is in front of you exactly, never letting a figure go unchecked.
